extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
extraction.description: The Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) is a reading comprehension dataset consisting of questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage. The paper states that SQuAD contains 107,785 question-answer pairs on 536 articles.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar; Jian Zhang; Konstantin Lopyrev; Percy Liang
extraction.citeAs: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, and Percy Liang. 2016. SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in three stages: curating passages from English Wikipedia articles, crowdsourcing question-answer pairs on those passages, and obtaining additional answers for development and test questions. The authors used Project Nayuki’s Wikipedia internal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 English Wikipedia articles, sampled 536 articles uniformly at random, extracted individual paragraphs, and then employed crowdworkers via the Daemo platform with Amazon Mechanical Turk as backend to write and answer questions on each paragraph.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator; Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English Wikipedia articles. Specifically, the authors used Project Nayuki’s Wikipedia internal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia, sampled 536 articles, and extracted individual paragraphs from those articles.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers created question-answer pairs for Wikipedia paragraphs by asking and answering up to 5 questions per paragraph; questions were entered in a text field and answers highlighted in the paragraph. Workers were given a sample paragraph and examples of good and bad questions and answers, were encouraged to ask questions in their own words without copying phrases, and copy-paste on the paragraph text was disabled. For development and test sets, additional crowdworkers were shown only the questions and paragraphs and asked to select the shortest span answering each question, or submit the question without marking an answer if no span answered it.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human performance was estimated using interannotator agreement: each question in development and test had at least three answers, the second answer was treated as the human prediction, and the other answers were kept as ground truth answers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: located in the United States or Canada
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Ignoring punctuation and articles, 77.3% of the correct answers in the development set are constituents. This places an effective ceiling on the accuracy of our methods.; Questions with span-based answers are more constrained than the more interpretative questions found in more advanced standardized tests.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: We have made our dataset freely available to encourage exploration of more expressive models.; We expect that the remaining gap will be harder to close, but that such efforts will result in significant advances in reading comprehension.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: reading comprehension; machine comprehension of text; training and evaluating models for reading comprehension/question answering
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: From each of these articles, we extracted individual paragraphs, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters. We partitioned the articles randomly into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: From each of these articles, we extracted individual paragraphs, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.
